gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Presented with 'So' as a consequence, but the preceding sentences only require q not to divide denominators; nothing given implies anything about numerators, and the page does not say which 'finitely many matrices' are meant or why numerators matter (e.g. for inverting F_1, F_2 modulo q^b).

gaps.term: why the update needs an interchange
gaps.quote: takes one interchange of two equal fields and two additions
gaps.note: The page never says which field additions are linear-cost and which are not, so the reader cannot see why D_tau <- D_tau + H_sigma counts as cheap O(V) work while the direct update H_sigma <- H_sigma + D_tau must be routed through an interchange.

Following the three stated operations: D becomes zeta+eta, the swap gives (zeta+eta, eta), and D <- D - H gives eta-(eta+zeta) = -zeta. The pair becomes (eta+zeta, -zeta), not (eta+zeta, zeta), so the reader cannot confirm D is left unchanged.

gaps.quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: Pi has rank M ones, one update per 1 and one interchange per update, which gives rank M interchanges, not 2 rank M; the last paragraph also counts the network's interchanges as the sum of the ranks. The reader cannot reconcile the factor 2.

The 'rank budget' is never defined beyond 'counts dimension changes along its edges', and the page does not say how edge ranks relate to wires, source projections and lost dimension, so the reader cannot derive or check this identity; it is not marked as cited.
